root_cause.location: rust/src/rl_d170a_option_policy_env.rs, D170a-specific composition layer (not the frozen `mod inherited` vocabulary block)
root_cause.defect: off-by-one in the resource `_trig` arm arming check: refresh_candidates() compares self.opp_worker_trigger_turn (captured pre-increment, inside step_one_turn, before that turn's engine step() call advances self.game.turn) against self.game.turn, but refresh_candidates() is only ever evaluated either before that turn's step_one_turn call (not yet set) or on the next loop iteration after game.turn has already advanced past the stored value -- structurally unreachable for any trajectory/seed. OPT_RETURN in the same file correctly handles the equivalent post-step timing via a sticky return_pending flag; the same pattern was not applied to the three resource _trig arms.
evidence: static code trace of the sole enqueue site (refresh_candidates, ~line 1149)
8/8 independent fits show exact zero (not stochastic rarity) for all three trig arms
D169a's own frozen hash-verified reference implementation of the identical vocabulary shows nonzero trig activity (opt_fruit_trig 25/1024, opt_iron_trig 13/1024 hindsight-envelope winners)
direct field-level diagnostic on the real D170a training pool: opp_worker_trigger_seen true in 451/2880 (15.7%) of observed decisions, yet trig_candidate_offered = 0/2880

decision_tree_branch_applied: Phase 1 mechanics-fail on all fits -> CLOSE (record; Tier 0/3)
verdict_rationale: All 8 Phase 1 fits deterministically and reproducibly fail the protocol's own pre-registered Stage-A mechanics gate (every_option_at_least_2pct_of_sampled_decisions), root-caused to a structural bug (not a rarity/threshold judgment call) in the new D170a sequential-decision composition code that makes 3 of the declared 13 arms permanently unreachable. No fit has decision=='trained'; there is no valid checkpoint to evaluate in Phase 2, and running Phase 2/3 on a fit trained over a silently-truncated 10-arm vocabulary would test a different, mislabeled experiment. Per the protocol's explicit prohibitions (no architecture/mechanics tuning after outcomes; frozen modules untouched) the resuming agent did not patch the bug and re-run -- that requires a new dispatch/authorization. This is a distinct decision-tree branch from Phase 2's own 'no admission' close and is recorded as such.
